session_summary: Large session: processed pending reflections (PR #45 v3.14.1 — 3 strong-signal template improvements + 9 reflections marked processed) and ran a full cost-optimization pass (research+audit+plan → docs, then implemented Tier A+B as PR #46 v3.15.0: prompt-cache prefix relocation, CLAUDE.md/bd-prime de-dup, exclude-dynamic-sections, staggered batch fan-out, per-agent max_turns). agent_feedback.worked_well: Excellent surgical discipline on the cost-opt dispatch-path edits (A1-A5): preserved all other behavior, did byte-level identity proofs, respected no-commit boundaries, and correctly refused to falsify a historical version tag during the docs bump.
agent_feedback.needs_improvement: On the reflection-apply task, harness-engineer hit max_turns (30) doing multi-file edits (templates.js + 9 reflection JSONs) and never emitted [DONE] — though the work had actually landed (verified on host). Multi-file 'apply + mark processed' tasks need a higher budget or splitting.
agent_feedback.suggested_change: For reflection-processing / multi-file mark-and-edit tasks, dispatch with max_turns 40+, or split the template edits from the processed:true marking. The agent template could also note: do the edits first, validate cheaply, and leave bulk file-stamping last so a turn-limit doesn't lose the substantive work.

agent_feedback.worked_well: Reliable explicit-path staging across many PRs — consistently excluded unrelated untracked files (cost docs vs reflection docs) and verified the staged set before committing.

overall_notes: Recurring orchestrator friction worth a template note: my version-bump validation criteria (stale==0 for old version strings) were too strict twice — agents correctly refused because the 'stale' hit was a legitimate historical feature-attribution tag (vX.Y.Z: in changelog prose), not the current-version badge. The validation clause should target the current-version badge specifically and explicitly allow historical version tags to remain. Batch result compaction (MAX_TAIL_CHARS) and the new compact batch summary table worked well this session. Tools: bd/dolt, gh, docker, node.
